general_information.Description: At the end of this course, students will be able to: 1.Background Knowledge: (ABET e) - Understand the role and functions of an operating system. - Grasp important OS concepts such as kernels, file systems, and process management. - Comprehend the mechanisms of operating systems, including memory hierarchy and CPU roles. - Identify and analyze main problems and challenges in operating systems. 2.Practical Skills: (ABET k) - Use basic and advanced shell commands in a Linux system fluently. - Develop proficiency in shell scripting on Linux. - Address and solve key operating system problems through practical exercises and simulations. 3.Information Searching, Reading, and Selection Skills: (ABET i) - Efficiently search for, read, and select relevant information related to operating systems and Linux. 4.Teamwork, Documentation, and Presentation Skills: (ABET g) - Work effectively in groups to complete projects. - Document and present findings and solutions clearly and professionally.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. - Student is responsible to do all exercises given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time - Use laptop in class only for learning purpose - Promptly access to the FU LMS https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/ for up-to-date course information
general_information.Tools: - Internet - Linux (CentOS, Ubuntu) operating system server and/or client

description: At the end of this course, students will be able to: 1.Background Knowledge: (ABET e) - Understand the role and functions of an operating system. - Grasp important OS concepts such as kernels, file systems, and process management. - Comprehend the mechanisms of operating systems, including memory hierarchy and CPU roles. - Identify and analyze main problems and challenges in operating systems. 2.Practical Skills: (ABET k) - Use basic and advanced shell commands in a Linux system fluently. - Develop proficiency in shell scripting on Linux. - Address and solve key operating system problems through practical exercises and simulations. 3.Information Searching, Reading, and Selection Skills: (ABET i) - Efficiently search for, read, and select relevant information related to operating systems and Linux. 4.Teamwork, Documentation, and Presentation Skills: (ABET g) - Work effectively in groups to complete projects. - Document and present findings and solutions clearly and professionally.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Grasp the core concepts of operating systems, including the kernel, process management, memory management, and file systems.
Understand how operating systems manage resources within the context of Linux.
Utilize the command line to operate and administer the Linux system.
Master regular expressions and shell scripting to automate tasks and manage system operations.
Develop advanced practical skills in Linux system administration.
Learn and implement basic security solutions on Linux systems.
Configure and understand TCP/IP networking protocols.
Set up and manage services on Linux systems.
Use AI, standard tools and techniques to manage, maintain, and troubleshoot Linux systems.

assessments.Note: The lab report content can be obtained from the lab manual, the lab templates, or created by the instructor to align with the chapters.

assessments.Question Type: Multiple choices marked by computer or a suitable format
assessments.No Question: 10 - 60 (At least 10*n questions, where n is the number of chapters covered in the test.)
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Current chapter(s). Each progress test covers at least 01 chapter and at most 06 chapter, and overall they must cover all learned chapters of the course.
assessments.Note: Instructions and schedules for progress tests must be included in the course implementation plan, which requires approval from the campus director. Progress tests should be administered immediately following the last lectures covering the required material. Instructors are responsible for reviewing the graded tests with students.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Students can either choose a topic themselves or refer to a list of topics suggested by lecturers.
assessments.Grading Guide: Prepare at home, work in groups, and present during class hours

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1.3
constructive_questions.Details: What are the primary advantages of Linux that make it a preferred choice for servers and developers

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1.4
constructive_questions.Details: How did GNU's tools and philosophies shape the Linux operating system?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ1.5
constructive_questions.Details: How can mastering the shell and command line enhance productivity for Linux users?

constructive_questions.Details: How can redirection (e.g., input, output, and error redirection) be leveraged for advanced file manipulation in Bash?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2.4
constructive_questions.Details: What are some effective ways to customize the Bash environment to match specific workflow needs?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ2.5
constructive_questions.Details: Why is “vi” still relevant today, and what advantages does it offer as a text editor for command-line users?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3.3
constructive_questions.Details: What is the difference between . and .. ?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3.4
constructive_questions.Details: Is the command mv foo1.txt foo2.txt a movement or a renaming operation? How do you know?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ3.5
constructive_questions.Details: How does the -i option differ between cp and rm?

constructive_questions.Details: Compare a program and a process. Why do we need two different terms to describe them?

constructive_questions.Details: Batch processing comes closest to which of these forms of processing, single tasking, preemptive multitasking or multiprocessing?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6.1
constructive_questions.Details: How can make this script more robust by handling potential errors and unexpected input gracefully?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6.2
constructive_questions.Details: Is there a more efficient or readable way to perform this repetitive task or complex logic using built-in shell commands or utilities?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6.3
constructive_questions.Details: How can parameterize this script to make it more reusable and adaptable to different scenarios?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6.4
constructive_questions.Details: How can I improve the maintainability and clarity of this script for myself and others who might need to understand or modify it in the future?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ6.5
constructive_questions.Details: How can I test this script thoroughly to ensure it behaves as expected in various situations and edge cases?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7.1
constructive_questions.Details: Why is it important to differentiate between root, user, and software accounts in a Linux system? Discuss the potential risks of improper management of these accounts.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7.2
constructive_questions.Details: Why is it crucial to enforce strong password policies in a Linux environment? Discuss the theoretical framework behind password strength and its impact on overall system security.

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7.3
constructive_questions.Details: Discuss the role and importance of Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM) in Linux. How do PAMs enhance security and flexibility in managing authentication methods?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7.4
constructive_questions.Details: How would you modify the ‘useradd’ command to create a new user with a non-default home directory and a specified shell?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ7.5
constructive_questions.Details: Describe a scenario where you would need to use the ‘chage’ command in Linux. What options would you use to enforce a password change policy for a specific user?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.1
constructive_questions.Details: Describe the role of an inode within Linux file systems. What metadata does an inode store, and why is this information critical for file system operations?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.2
constructive_questions.Details: Theoretically, why might an administrator choose to use multiple partitions on a Linux system? What are the benefits of partitioning a disk in terms of system security and data management?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.3
constructive_questions.Details: Compare the file allocation table (FAT) system to the inode-based system used in Linux. What are the benefits of using inodes over FAT, particularly in terms of file access and system performance?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.4
constructive_questions.Details: Explain the significance of journaling in file systems like ext4 and XFS. How does journaling enhance data integrity and system reliability after crashes or power failures?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ8.5
constructive_questions.Details: Explain the differences and use cases for block storage, file storage, and object storage within a Linux environment. How does each impact system performance and scalability?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ9.1
constructive_questions.Details: How can you verify and analyze each stage of the Linux boot process to identify potential failures?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ9.2
constructive_questions.Details: If your system fails to boot and only displays a GRUB prompt, what steps would you take to manually boot into Linux?

constructive_questions.Details: How can you use journalctl and dmesg to troubleshoot boot issues and identify failing services?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ12.1
constructive_questions.Details: Assume you back up your hard disk every week. Is there a reason to retain a week- old backup when you replace it with the next week’s backup? If so, why?

constructive_questions.Details: What is the advantage of using incremental backups rather than full backups? What is the disadvantage of using incremental backups?

constructive_questions.Name: CQ12.3
constructive_questions.Details: You have three tapes to store backups on. You plan to put a full backup on one tape and then incremental backups on the other two tapes doing the incremental backups every other day. You estimate that you can place 4 incremental backups on each tape. How many days will it be before you run out of tapes and must overwrite the full backup on the first tape?
